title: Lean claim manifest
description: Renderer-neutral record of manuscript claims backed by machine-checked Lean declarations. Populated only from human-authored mapping.toml entries (see t24.1 blocker B1) — nothing here is inferred from name or notation similarity.

content_hash.description: sha256 hex digest of the canonical JSON encoding of `claims`, computed identically by both renderer bindings so they can be proven to share one manifest.

paper.description: Project directory name under src/latex/projects, e.g. '03_distance_implied_mpt'.

claim_id.description: Stable human-authored identifier for the manuscript claim, e.g. a label key. Never a Lean identifier.

statement_summary.description: Plain-language statement of the mathematical claim, independent of Lean notation.

package.description: Lake sub-package name under src/lean/packages, e.g. 'EnergyStatistics'.

file.description: Path to the declaring file relative to src/lean, e.g. 'packages/EnergyStatistics/EnergyStatistics/VStatistic.lean'.

build_result.description: Set by the extractor from the pinned Lake workspace build — never hand-authored as 'checked'.

assumptions.description: Named hypotheses / Prop-valued premises the theorem statement carries (not Lean axioms).

axioms.description: Axiom set reported by `#print axioms <declaration>`. A build_result of 'checked' implies this is a subset of the allowlist {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound} and does not contain sorryAx.

statement_type.description: Elaborated type reported by `#check @<declaration>`, whitespace-collapsed so it is stable under pretty-printer line breaking. Pins the statement rather than only the declaration name: because it is hashed into content_hash, weakening a mapped theorem in place produces a visible manifest diff instead of silently leaving a stale disclosure attached to a weaker result. Empty only on a 'failed' claim whose type could not be recovered.

disclosure.description: Human-facing sentence describing exactly what was verified, safe to surface next to the manuscript claim.
